DONE, with one scope boundary stated below rather than glossed.

Introduced in core/StructuredResult.scala:
- ResultPlan[A](schema, contract, maximumResultBytes, maximumEnvelopeBytes, declaredOutputs)
- PreparedJob[A](launch: LaunchSpec, resultPlan: ResultPlan[A], digest: ContentDigest)
- PreparedAttempt[A](job, attemptId, epoch, operation, workerRelease), with durableHandle(bound)

The reviewer's refinement is honoured and it earns its keep: PreparedJob carries NO attempt identity. A retry is a new attempt at the SAME prepared job, so baking an attempt in would force re-preparation and re-digesting of a launch that never changed. A test pins this — a retried attempt shares the identical PreparedJob and digest.

The substance is that DurableResultHandle is now DERIVED. It was being constructed beside the plan, in two places in RegisteredTaskLauncher, from overlapping facts — nothing prevented a handle advertising one schema, byte limit or output set while the plan that reads the result used another. durableHandle projects the plan, so the two cannot disagree. A property over generated outputs, limits and bindings asserts exactly that agreement.

DESIGN CORRECTION made during implementation: my first ResultPlan took a ResultCodec[A] and derived the schema from it. That is wrong here. The OPERATION names the result schema, not the contract — an exit-only contract has no schema of its own, yet the attempt still has one to record, and OperationRef carries a descriptor rather than a codec. ResultPlan therefore holds the schema explicitly alongside the typed contract.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, stated plainly: one of the two launcher construction sites is wired to derive its handle (RegisteredTaskLauncher, the typed registered-task path). The second site (the remote registered path, ~:501) still constructs a DurableResultHandle directly. It has all the facts locally and is mechanical to convert, but it belongs with the remote-path restructuring in D6/D7 rather than being half-migrated here. The type-level guarantee holds wherever PreparedAttempt is used; it is not yet used everywhere.

Also not done here, and correctly D3/D6 work: typed results are still recovered by runtime ResultSchemaId equality (ssh/RemoteTask.scala:336, managed/ResultAttachment.scala:58) rather than through PreparedAttempt. D2 gives that path a typed home to move into; it does not move it.

Verification: full suite 415 (411 + 4 new PreparedAttemptSuite) green, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.
